newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Brazil co-op sees 24-25 mln bag coffee crop '97/98.
newsitem.headline: Brazil co-op sees 24-25 mln bag coffee crop '97/98.

text.p: Brazil's largest co-operative said on Wednesday the country's coffee crop should reach 24 to 25 million 60-kg bags in 1997/98, down only slightly from 1996/97, if the coffee areas escape winter frost.

"We should have 24-25 million bags for the 1997/98 season, if we don't have any weather problem in the next one and a half months," Joaquim Libanio Ferreira Leite, export director of Cooperativa Regional de Cafeicultores Em Guaxupe lta, told Reuters during a coffee conference in Vienna.
"If we have a frost, you are going to see a real damage for the industry in my country especially now we don't have any stocks," he added.
He gave no further details. His estimate was within earlier trade expectations, although forecasts from other Brazilian sources put the crop at 20 million or below.
Recent estimates of the 1996/97 crop range around 27-30 million bags.

The association is Brazil's leading coffee growers' co-operative and the country's second biggest exporter. It has 7,000 members of which 80 percent are smallholders. In the 1996/97 season it traded two million bags of which 850,000 were exported.
